title: Hydrochloric Acid
page_title: Role of Hydrochloric Acid in Digestion - IGCSE Biology Notes

blocks.name: Hydrochloric acid
blocks.definition: Describe the functions of hydrochloric acid in gastric juice, limited to killing harmful microorganisms in food and providing an acidic pH for optimum enzyme activity

blocks.md:
- The stomach produces several fluids which together are known as **gastric juice**
- One of the fluids produced is **hydrochloric acid**
- This **kills bacteria** in food and gives an **acid pH for enzymes** to work in the stomach

blocks.text: How is a low pH helpful in the stomach?

blocks.md:
- The low pH kills bacteria in ingested food as it **denatures the enzymes in their cells**, meaning they cannot carry out any cell reactions to maintain life
- [Pepsin](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/biology/cie/23/revision-notes/7-human-nutrition/7-1-human-diet-and-digestion/7-1-11-digestion-of-protein/?_ai=internal-linking), produced in the stomach, is an example of an enzyme which has a very low optimum pH - around **pH 2**
- The hydrochloric acid produced in the stomach ensures that conditions in the **stomach remain within the optimum** range for pepsin to work at its fastest rate
